active_paradigms.idea: Replica-aware group-to-node packing using a water-filling surrogate
active_paradigms.description: The current code packs groups to nodes using raw group token sums, then decides replicas separately inside each node. This misses the key interaction: a node receiving a concentrated hot expert can dissipate that load through its available replica slots, whereas a node receiving several moderately hot experts may remain harder to balance. Before the existing node packing, compute a replica-aware effective group cost by estimating the best attainable maximum per-replica stream for each candidate node allocation, using integer water-filling on the experts in that group. Use this effective cost, rather than raw group sum, as the weight passed to the existing capacity-constrained LPT packing. The calculation can be implemented tensor-wise by sorting expert loads and evaluating the finite set of thresholds induced by load divided by replica count; no MILP, flow, or assignment solver is needed. Retain the existing hierarchy and output construction, so all placement invariants and rank semantics remain unchanged. This directly improves the first hierarchical decision, which otherwise irreversibly constrains every later replica and GPU decision. It is especially valuable when expert load is highly skewed and replicas are plentiful relative to the number of nodes.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Reduce worst node pressure and downstream GPU imbalance by making node group assignment reflect replica capacity; preserve the current vectorized runtime profile.
active_paradigms.cautions: The surrogate must respect the exact fixed number of physical slots per node, including the mandatory first copy of every expert. Do not change group membership unless evaluator constraints explicitly permit it. Use float32 only for ordering/estimation and preserve integer maps. Since the underlying evaluator is not shown in the supplied wrapper, validate both balance score and execution time on every workload rather than assuming a raw-load surrogate is always beneficial.

active_paradigms.idea: Bounded largest-smallest exchange refinement after LPT GPU packing
active_paradigms.description: The final GPU placement is cardinality-constrained LPT: each replica stream is placed once, in descending order, onto the least-loaded non-full GPU. LPT is fast but can leave a large stream paired with medium streams while another GPU contains several streams whose aggregate is only slightly smaller. Add a strictly bounded local improvement pass that considers only the heaviest loaded GPU and lightest loaded GPU in each layer, selects a small fixed candidate set of their largest and smallest streams, and accepts the best feasible one-for-one swap only if it decreases the layer maximum GPU load. Evaluate swap deltas analytically from the current GPU sums, so candidate scoring is a small batched tensor operation rather than rebuilding an assignment or calling a solver. Repeat for at most a fixed 2–4 rounds, or until no improving swap exists. Because every GPU keeps exactly `phy_experts_per_gpu` streams, this refinement preserves all output shape and placement constraints. Unlike the failed min-cost-flow and Hungarian approaches, this optimizes the actual nonlinear bottleneck produced by a complete placement and uses LPT as a strong warm start rather than replacing it with a linear proxy.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Lower the per-layer peak physical-GPU replica load, which is the likely load-balance bottleneck, with predictable bounded overhead.
active_paradigms.cautions: Never swap replica identities in a way that loses `phyrank`; carry stream indices and gather both `phy2mlog` and `phyrank` from the refined permutation. Use strict improvement with a small epsilon to avoid oscillation and deterministic tie breaking for reproducibility. Limit candidate and iteration counts aggressively because the evaluator has a runtime component and runs single-threaded. Do not use full all-pairs GPU/stream search, which can erase the vectorization advantage of the current implementation.

active_paradigms.idea: Exact discrete threshold water-filling for replica-count allocation
active_paradigms.description: The present replica allocator repeatedly gives the next slot to the expert with largest current `weight/count`. That greedy rule is good for minimizing the largest isolated replica stream, but it does not explicitly solve the fixed-budget minimax count allocation and can be sensitive to ties and subsequent GPU cardinality packing. Replace the sequential extra-slot loop with a threshold formulation: for a candidate stream-load threshold T, expert e requires `ceil(weight[e]/T)` copies, clipped to the available maximum; the smallest feasible T is found among the discrete breakpoints `weight[e]/k`. Select the minimum threshold whose required-copy sum fits the physical-expert budget, then distribute any leftover slots to the experts with greatest reduction from one additional copy. This gives a globally consistent minimax replica-count vector for each node/layer before GPU packing, while avoiding a Python loop over every redundant slot. Generate breakpoint ordering and leftover priorities in batched tensors, then construct `phy2log` and ranks from counts by masked sorting. This is fundamentally different from the failed MILP attempts: it exploits the separable reciprocal load structure exactly rather than expressing a weak linearized proxy. It can also be faster than the current method when there are many redundant physical slots.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Improve replica-count quality for the maximum per-copy load objective and reduce allocation cost when replica surplus is large.
active_paradigms.cautions: Counts must remain at least one for every logical expert and sum exactly to physical slots within each node; zero-weight experts need deterministic handling because their threshold breakpoint is zero. The threshold objective alone does not account for final GPU packing, so compare it against current greedy allocation and keep the better result using an inexpensive predicted post-packing maximum if benchmark distributions are heterogeneous. Ensure the constructed replica ranks are contiguous from zero through count minus one, otherwise `log2phy.scatter_` validation/output semantics will break.

tried_paradigms.idea: Solve the per-layer replica-count and placement problem directly with a bounded mixed-integer linear program
tried_paradigms.description: The current program first greedily assigns whole logical groups to nodes, then greedily chooses replicas by largest current weight/count, and finally applies LPT packing to GPUs. This is fast and produces valid maps, but its three irreversible greedy stages optimize local proxies rather than the final maximum GPU load. Formulate a small per-layer MILP with binary assignment variables for physical slots, constraints that every logical expert has at least one replica, exactly `num_replicas` slots are filled, each GPU receives `num_replicas / num_gpus` slots, and replica rank/count consistency is maintained when emitting the maps. Add a continuous variable `T` and constrain each GPU's summed per-replica expected load to be at most `T`; if hierarchical locality is required by the original evaluator, restrict every expert's copies to the node selected for its group. Use the current greedy solution as an incumbent/warm start if supported, impose a strict small time limit, and retain the greedy result whenever the MILP does not prove or find an improvement quickly. This directly attacks the likely load-balance portion of the combined score rather than optimizing the intermediate group and replica proxies. The evaluator adapter only exposes `combined_score`, not its formula, so inspect the imported original evaluator before deciding whether node-load constraints must also be included in the MILP objective.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Final per-GPU maximum load and tail imbalance, while using a hard solve-time cutoff so improved balance does not lose more combined score through runtime.
tried_paradigms.cautions: A full binary formulation can be too large for all layers/configurations; apply it only below a variable-count threshold and fall back to the present vectorized greedy algorithm. The emitted `phy2log`, `phyrank`, `logcnt`, and padded `log2phy` must remain mutually consistent, including experts with only one copy. Do not optimize a fractional relaxation and round it without repair, because capacity and replica-count violations can invalidate evaluator results.

tried_paradigms.idea: Replace the final LPT GPU packing with a single min-cost-flow assignment using convex load-slot costs
tried_paradigms.description: The existing `balanced_packing` is capacity-constrained LPT: it sorts replicas by load and sends each next replica to the currently least-loaded non-full GPU. Its strength is deterministic speed, but it cannot reconsider early heavyweight placements and can be noticeably suboptimal when several replicas have similar large loads. Keep the existing group-to-node and replica-count stages, then build one flow network independently for each layer-node: each physical replica is one unit of supply, each GPU has exactly `phy_experts_per_gpu` position nodes, and all GPU positions feed the sink with unit capacity. Give the arc from replica `i` to the k-th position of GPU `g` a discretized marginal cost derived from a convex penalty around the target GPU load, with later positions on a GPU increasingly expensive. Run one `networkx.min_cost_flow` call to obtain a globally capacity-feasible assignment rather than sequential LPT decisions. Calibrate the marginal-cost scale from the actual replica loads and target total-load/number-of-GPUs, so the flow minimizes a close surrogate for squared overload or maximum-load excess. Convert the resulting selected replica-to-position arcs into the same `pphy2phy` permutation currently consumed by the map construction. This is structurally different from changing replication: it preserves valid counts but improves the last placement decision where the evaluator is most likely to observe imbalance.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: GPU-level load dispersion after replication, especially cases where LPT's earliest assignments create an avoidable overloaded GPU.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Flow costs must be nonnegative integers for reliable NetworkX min-cost flow use; scale floats conservatively and use deterministic rounding. The load-slot surrogate is not exactly a nonlinear makespan objective, so compare its predicted maximum load with LPT and keep LPT if flow is worse. Graph size grows with replicas times GPUs times slots, so use this only for moderate per-node instances or use a coarse set of load slots.

tried_paradigms.idea: Deduplicate exactly equal layer load vectors before rebalancing and expand the maps afterward
tried_paradigms.description: The current code vectorizes across layers but still performs every sort, greedy replica decision, and packing loop for every layer, even when workload collection contains repeated load histograms. Since all operations are deterministic functions of one row of `weight` and the topology parameters, identical rows necessarily have identical optimal greedy outputs. Before calling either hierarchy path, use `torch.unique(weight, dim=0, return_inverse=True)` to retain only distinct layer rows, run the existing high-quality algorithm once on that compact matrix, and index the three output tensors by `return_inverse` to restore original layer order. This preserves every output value exactly relative to the current program for duplicate rows, so it has no correctness or load-balance trade-off. It can substantially reduce wall time when many MoE layers share a routing distribution, are zero-load, or workload traces are repeated, which can improve the combined score even if the evaluator's balance metric is unchanged. Extend the same idea to an all-zero-row fast path if that is common, because any valid canonical placement is balance-equivalent for such rows. This exploits an important property the current batched implementation does not exploit: vectorization avoids Python overhead but does not avoid repeated algorithmic work.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Algorithm execution time with exactly unchanged expert placement quality for repeated rows; this is the lowest-risk way to improve a combined quality/runtime score.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Only exact equality is safe unless the evaluator explicitly tolerates approximate map changes; do not quantize or cluster near-equal weights. `torch.unique(dim=0)` may itself cost time and memory, so activate it only when the number of layers is sufficiently large or a cheap duplicate check indicates repetition. Preserve CPU device, integer dtypes, and inverse-index ordering when expanding `phy2log`, `log2phy`, and `logcnt`.

tried_paradigms.idea: Solve per-layer replica-count and GPU-placement choices jointly with SciPy HiGHS MILP
tried_paradigms.description: The displayed adapter only returns the original evaluator's aggregate result, so its exact balance/time formula is not visible here; inspect that imported evaluator before choosing a solver cutoff. The current program first fixes node groups, then greedily chooses replica counts by largest current weight/count, and finally uses capacity-constrained LPT to assign already-fixed replicas to GPUs. This is fast and valid, but it cannot undo a poor replica decision when that decision creates an unbalanced GPU partition. For small and medium layer configurations, formulate one independent `scipy.optimize.milp` per layer with binary variables representing a choice of replica count k for each expert and assignment of its k copies to GPU slots. Precompute each copy's load as weight[e]/k, require exactly one k per expert, exactly k selected copy placements when k is selected, and exactly physical-experts-per-GPU copies on every GPU. Add a continuous makespan variable T and constraints that each GPU's selected copy-load sum is at most T; preserve the hierarchical policy by only allowing an expert's copies on GPUs belonging to its assigned node. Minimize T with a very small secondary linear term favoring fewer disruptive changes or deterministic slot order, then reconstruct `phy2log`, ranks, counts, and the padded inverse map exactly as required. Use this only below a conservative variable-count threshold and retain the current vectorized greedy method as fallback for large instances.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Directly minimizes maximum expected GPU expert load, which is the weakness of separate greedy replication and LPT placement; use it when evaluator balance gains outweigh solver runtime.
tried_paradigms.cautions: The load contribution must be weight[e]/k for every selected copy, not weight[e], and rank values must be dense 0..k-1 per logical expert. MILP symmetry is substantial, so impose canonical copy ordering and a strict time limit; an untimed MILP can destroy the execution-time component or evaluator timeout. Do not use this if the evaluator requires a specific stable group ordering beyond node locality.

tried_paradigms.idea: Replace greedy LPT GPU packing with a single min-cost-flow assignment over replica streams and convex GPU load tiers
tried_paradigms.description: The current implementation's strongest feature is that replication allocation is cheap and mathematically equivalent to repeatedly choosing the largest weight/count stream. Its main placement weakness is that LPT decides each item against only the current least-loaded GPU, so it has no global view of which later heavy streams will compete for the same GPU. Keep the current group-to-node assignment and replica counts, because these preserve locality and make the output shape straightforward, but replace only the within-node physical-replica-to-GPU packing. Build a directed flow graph for each layer-node: every replica stream supplies one unit, every GPU has exactly its physical-expert capacity, and GPU capacity is represented by ordered unit-capacity tier arcs. Give replica-to-tier arcs costs based on a discretized convex overload penalty relative to the node's ideal total load, so expensive heavy assignments into already expensive tiers are discouraged. Solve the assignment in one call to `networkx.min_cost_flow`, decode each replica's GPU and position it within that GPU, and leave the existing logical rank/count reconstruction unchanged. This is globally optimized for the chosen convex surrogate rather than the myopic LPT objective and is especially useful when a few replicas remain much heavier than the rest.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Reduce post-replication per-GPU load variance and maximum overload without changing the locality-preserving node/group and replica-count stages; potentially improve balance at moderate runtime cost.
tried_paradigms.cautions: The flow graph must enforce one unit from every physical replica and exactly the required number of units into every GPU; otherwise it can silently leave slots unused. Costs should be bounded integer values because NetworkX min-cost flow is integer-cost based; scale float weights carefully and use deterministic tie breaking. This is slower than tensor LPT, so gate it to small per-node replica counts or only layers whose greedy predicted max load exceeds a threshold; never invoke it for every large layer blindly.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use a one-shot Hungarian assignment against load-targeted GPU slots after replica allocation
tried_paradigms.description: The existing final `balanced_packing` is a vectorized LPT heuristic: it is fast across layers but commits each descending replica to the currently lightest non-full pack. A distinct inexpensive alternative is to expand each GPU into its fixed number of physical-expert slots and solve a single rectangular assignment with `scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment` separately for each layer-node. Construct a cost matrix between replica streams and GPU slots using the evaluator-relevant expected replica load and a static convex target penalty: slots on each GPU receive increasing marginal prices around the target node load, with deterministic tiny perturbations for ties. Calibrate the slot price curve from the total replicated load divided by GPUs, so assigning a heavy stream to a late/high-price slot is much more costly than assigning it to an early slot. Hungarian assignment globally chooses all stream-slot pairings under exact capacity, unlike sequential LPT, while its cubic complexity can remain acceptable for typical per-node expert counts. Decode slot index into GPU and local physical position, preserving the existing replica stream identities and `phyrank`. This is a good middle ground when MILP is too expensive but greedy LPT leaves measurable imbalance.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Improve the global quality of GPU-slot placement while retaining the current fast greedy replica allocation and exact GPU capacity constraints.
tried_paradigms.cautions: A static assignment cost is a surrogate, not the exact squared load of a GPU, because actual GPU load couples all assigned streams; validate the target-price schedule against the real evaluator rather than assuming lower surrogate cost means a higher score. Ensure all slots are included exactly once and keep all assignments within their node when hierarchy is active. Hungarian is cubic in replicas per node and creates CPU arrays, so use it only when its measured runtime beats the score's runtime penalty, with current LPT as fallback.

tried_paradigms.idea: Replace final GPU LPT with a Hungarian assignment to equal-capacity GPU slots
tried_paradigms.description: The current program first uses LPT to pack logical groups to nodes, allocates replica counts by repeatedly splitting the largest weight/count stream, and then uses another greedy LPT pass to place the resulting physical replicas on GPUs. Its main strength is that replica allocation is close to optimal for minimizing the largest individual replica stream and all operations are batched across layers. Its main weakness is the final LPT placement: early large placements can make the fixed-cardinality GPU partitions unrecoverably uneven, especially when only a few replicas dominate a node. For each layer-node independently, create exactly `physical_experts_per_gpu` slots per local GPU and set a desired cumulative-load profile for each GPU using the average local physical load. Build a rectangular square cost matrix between physical replicas and slots where a replica-to-slot cost is the increase in squared deviation from that GPU's target, with slot costs increasing according to the load already represented by earlier slots. Solve the assignment once with `scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment`, then derive the local physical ordering from assigned slot indices and preserve `phyrank` unchanged. This is fundamentally different from the failed min-cost-flow attempt because it is a dense bipartite assignment with exact one-item/one-slot constraints, not a convex-flow relaxation, and it should only replace the final GPU packing rather than attempting to jointly formulate all decisions. Compare its resulting maximum GPU load and variance against LPT and retain the Hungarian result only when it improves the evaluator-relevant imbalance statistic.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: The per-GPU load tail within each node, especially max GPU load and load variance caused by greedy final placement; this should improve the load-balance component without changing replica counts or topology constraints.
tried_paradigms.cautions: A static slot cost is only a surrogate for cumulative bin load, so construct slots in increasing marginal-load order and validate against actual reconstructed GPU loads before accepting it. The matrix is per layer-node and can become expensive for very large local replica counts; use LPT as a size-based fallback. Do not alter the required `phy2log`, rank, or fixed experts-per-GPU cardinalities, since malformed maps likely receive a zero evaluator score.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use batched best-exchange descent instead of one-pass LPT for each packing level
tried_paradigms.description: The current greedy packer never revisits an earlier group or physical-replica choice, so its score is limited by local LPT mistakes rather than by replica-count allocation itself. Replace each use of `balanced_packing` with a direct exchange-based balanced partitioner: begin from a deterministic capacity-valid assignment and repeatedly identify the most-loaded and least-loaded pack for every batch row. Evaluate moving each eligible item from the heavy pack to the light pack and swapping it with an item from the light pack, choosing the operation that gives the largest lexicographic reduction in `(maximum pack load, sum of squared pack loads)`. Maintain pack loads and membership tensors incrementally, so each accepted operation uses scatter updates rather than recomputing all pack sums. Run only a very small fixed number of rounds, and stop a row as soon as no strictly improving move or swap exists; unlike a seed-and-refine pipeline, this is the packing algorithm itself. Apply it to group-to-node assignment and physical-to-GPU assignment, while retaining the current replica water-filling, whose repeated largest `weight/count` selection is already a strong and usually optimal discrete allocation rule for the max per-copy stream. The expected gain is greatest on layers with several nearly equal heavy objects where LPT tie/order effects matter.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Direct reduction of maximum node/GPU load and secondary load dispersion while respecting exactly equal object counts in every pack; it targets the principal greedy-quality limitation rather than adding more replicas.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Only accept strictly improving operations under a stable floating-point tolerance, otherwise equal-load swaps can cycle and damage runtime consistency. Moves must preserve `groups_per_pack` or `phy_experts_per_gpu`; for full packs, use swaps rather than illegal moves. Bound rounds tightly and vectorize candidate scoring, because a Python all-pairs search can lose any score gain if evaluator runtime is included. Reconstruct inverse permutations after every finalized assignment and test that every logical replica rank remains unique.

tried_paradigms.idea: Compile and fuse the batched greedy kernels so quality-preserving balancing costs substantially less
tried_paradigms.description: The evaluator wrapper explicitly forces a fresh serial, single-threaded process and imposes a finite timeout, so algorithm execution cost can affect the combined scalar even if mapping quality is unchanged. The current implementation avoids scalar conversions but still executes Python loops over every group and every redundant replica, each containing multiple tensor dispatches such as masked fill, argmin, gather, and scatter. Wrap the core packing and replica-allocation kernels in `torch.compile` with a fixed-shape-friendly mode, keeping all tensors on CPU and compiling only after input normalization. This permits TorchInductor to fuse repeated pointwise operations, reuse buffers, and reduce Python dispatch overhead while leaving the exact LPT decisions and output maps unchanged. Use a shape-specialized cache keyed by `(layers, logical_experts, replicas, groups, nodes, gpus)` so repeated evaluator workloads do not trigger recompilation. This is a different objective axis from assignment quality: it protects the existing 0.129100-quality behavior while creating time budget for a bounded exact/exchange packing variant on difficult shapes. If compilation startup dominates a one-shot evaluation, compile only when the estimated loop work exceeds a threshold and otherwise call the eager vectorized implementation.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Runtime and timeout robustness of the current high-quality vectorized LPT/water-filling algorithm, while preserving exactly the same maps and hence avoiding balance regressions.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Compilation can have substantial first-call latency in a fresh evaluator process, so benchmark end-to-end startup rather than kernel time alone. Guard this path with `hasattr(torch, 'compile')` and retain eager behavior if compilation fails or the installed PyTorch backend lacks Inductor support. Avoid data-dependent Python branching inside compiled kernels, and verify bitwise or tie-equivalent outputs because tiny floating-point changes in `argmin` ties can alter placement and evaluator load metrics.
